mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the Federal Funds rate above 5% for two consecutive months reduces the present value of future equity cash flows, thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 5% and remains above for two consecutive months
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns show no statistically significant negative relationship with FEDFUNDS changes (p > 0.05 in OLS), or the rate remains below 5% throughout the horizon.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) coincides with stronger consumer confidence (HOUST), creating a labor-market expansion signal that is associated with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS growth rate exceeds 50,000 jobs/month and HOUST exceeds 1,700 units in the same month
failure_condition: In a 60-day walk-forward, the correlation between combined labor indicators and SPX 20d returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05), or the labor signal occurs without market strength.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below 110 suggests weakening supply-side constraints, prompting investors to price in higher future demand and thus drive positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: Over 12 consecutive 5-day windows, INDPRO declines do not precede statistically significant positive SPX 5-day forward returns (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the ratio of industrial production to capacity (INDPRO normalized) falls below 85 for two consecutive months, it indicates underutilization of key manufacturing capacity, which is associated with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days as market anticipates a supply shock.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO normalized < 85 for two consecutive months
failure_condition: In 20 out of 20 instances of INDPRO normalization < 85, SPX 20d returns are non-negative (p < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) above 3% for three consecutive months triggers a preemptive rate hike expectation, which compresses discount rates and produces negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL crosses above 3% and remains above for three consecutive months
failure_condition: In 10 out of 20 inflation spikes, the 60-day SPX forward return is not statistically different from zero (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden drop in unemployment (UNRATE) below 4% coincides with a decline in labor market participation (PAYEMS), signaling a tight labor market that can drive short-term risk aversion and thus negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE falls below 4% in the same month that PAYEMS falls by >10,000 jobs
failure_condition: During 20 instances of dual labor signals, SPX 20d returns show no negative relationship (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When monthly retail sales (not in observable list - skip) cannot be used, instead: A sustained monthly increase in residential investment (not in observable list - fallback to demand proxy) is not directly observable; instead, use HOUST as a proxy for consumer sentiment. Thus, a sustained rise in HOUST above 1700 units for two months signals improving demand expectations and predicts positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST exceeds 1700 for two consecutive months
failure_condition: Over 12 consecutive 5-day windows, HOUST > 1700 does not precede positive SPX 5-day returns (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A prolonged decline in manufacturing activity (RSAFS) below 400 million dollars for three months indicates weakening industrial production, which is associated with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days as market anticipates supply constraints.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS falls below 400 for three consecutive months
failure_condition: In 15 out of 20 instances of RSAFS decline, SPX 60-day forward returns are non-negative (p < 0.05).
